Zaphira Nature.thesis: A salon-led curl and textured-hair brand built for Gulf heat and hard water. It has already moved from the UAE into Kuwait and, in October 2026, Saudi Arabia.
Zaphira Nature.why: Haircare sits outside Huda Beauty's core and is the region's fastest-growing beauty category. A female founder fits the HB Angels mandate. Salons give it trust; HBI could add the content reach salons cannot.
risks: Curly and textured hair is a focused niche, so the addressable market needs sizing.
Salon distribution builds slowly and depends on stylist goodwill.
A 5.3K Instagram audience is small for a three-market brand.
q: What is the revenue split across salons, retail and online?
How often do salons reorder, and what is sell-through per salon?
What are the terms of the Saudi launch partner?
What is gross margin after salon consignment?

MZN Bodycare.thesis: Saudi natural body care with distribution most young brands would envy: 80+ retail partners, Faces and pharmacy chains. Its social presence lags far behind its shelf presence.
MZN Bodycare.why: The gap between shelf and screen is exactly where a creator-led owner adds value. Saudi-made production also fits local-content tailwinds. The founder is female and the category does not overlap Huda Beauty.
risks: Founded in 2015, so it is not a young brand. Growth may have plateaued.
Handmade, micro-factory production may cap volume.
Value price points leave less room for marketing spend.
q: What is sell-through per door, and how concentrated are sales in the top 10 doors?
What is the production capacity ceiling today?
How do margins differ between Faces, pharmacies and online?
What has been tried on social so far, and what worked?

Nutrili.thesis: Beauty-from-within supplements (gummy vitamins, marine collagen) that have just moved from online-only to shelves at Spinneys, and sell on Ounass in three markets.
Nutrili.why: Wellness is a natural neighbour to beauty. It complements HBI's Humantra (hydration) without overlapping it. A female founder with 20,000+ customers across 15 countries is a proven seller.
risks: Supplement rules differ by GCC market and slow expansion.
A second brand (JUST Snacks) can split founder focus.
Instagram engagement could not be read, so momentum is unproven here.
q: What is the repeat purchase rate, and how much revenue is subscription?
What does it cost to acquire a customer online today?
Which market approvals are in hand, and which are pending?
How is time split between Nutrili and JUST Snacks?

Passion Labs.thesis: An Arabic-first, chemist-founded natural skin, hair and soap brand, made in the UAE, with a real community around it.
Passion Labs.why: Its 0.54% engagement on 21.9K followers is the second-best momentum among brands of its size. It speaks to an Arabic-speaking audience Huda Beauty knows well, and no outside money is disclosed.
risks: Only one verified retailer, so it depends on direct sales.
Little public information on the founder, team or revenue.
The natural-care space is crowded with small local makers.
q: What are revenue and repeat rates today?
How is production set up, and can it scale?
What are the founder's ambitions: regional brand or local favourite?
Which retailers have approached it?

Gaudia Beauty.thesis: Dates-infused scalp and hair treatments, launched in 2024, with the strongest momentum on the list and a new travel-size Mini Set (October 2026).
Gaudia Beauty.why: A classic HB Angels profile: very early, female founder, heritage ingredient, fastest-growing category, no outside money. Small enough that HBI support would matter.
risks: A 2.9K audience means strong engagement may not hold at scale.
q: What are sales to date, and through which channels?
Which retailers are in the pipeline?
Where is it manufactured, and at what minimum order size?
How much capital does the next 12 months need, and for what?
